implemented: A shared bounded upstream-response reader rejects an oversized valid Content-Length before reading and treats measured stream bytes as authoritative when Content-Length is absent, invalid, or false.

The reader cancels rejected streams, releases reader locks, uses fatal UTF-8 decoding, and returns structured sanitized failures for size, stream, abort, and encoding errors without exposing upstream bytes.
The managed-model provider response budget is 32768 base bytes plus 64 bytes per configured max output token, with the token input bounded to 16384 and an absolute 1048576-byte response cap.
WeChat Pay and Stripe response bodies both use a fixed 65536-byte cap before signature verification or JSON parsing.

The public HTTP mirror origin http://47.93.180.216 was removed from both sensitive Function default CORS allowlists. Wildcards, opaque null origins, unknown origins, public HTTP aliases, and unsafe configured allowlists fail closed.

The HTTP mirror remains available for anonymous public viewing and versioned downloads, while account, console, managed-model, community-write, and checkout entries are disabled before a sensitive request can be issued.
Existing bearer-token, grant, callback-signature, idempotency, and provider-verification controls remain in place; CORS is explicitly not treated as authentication.
scope.excluded: No Supabase Function, production secret, CORS environment variable, payment or model-provider configuration, DNS, TLS, server, GitHub Release, GitHub Pages, Alibaba Cloud site, installer, runtime, backend, or technical-report state was deployed or changed.

securityDesign.contentLength: A valid announced size over the route limit is rejected before body consumption. Any missing, invalid, or smaller announced size never weakens the measured stream-byte limit.
securityDesign.streaming: ReadableStream chunks are counted before decoding; a measured overrun cancels the reader. All completion and rejection paths release the reader lock.
securityDesign.errorPrivacy: Call points log only a structured rejection code or provider status. They never log or return an upstream response body, credential, payment payload, or model text.
securityDesign.threatBoundary: CORS reduces browser-origin exposure but does not authenticate a caller. JWT, one-time model grants, payment signatures, RLS, provider signature checks, and server-side authorization remain required. A request without an Origin header is governed by those authentication and protocol controls, not by CORS.
